## Machine (shared by three agents)
32 threads (i9-14900KF), 23 GB RAM + 16 GB swap, RTX 4080 SUPER 16 GB, nvcc 12.0, g++ 13.3, ffmpeg. Everything runs inside a tmux memory cgroup: an OOM there kills the agent process. `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=XG <cmd>` works and gives a real cgroup limit.

**Proposed etiquette:** each agent caps itself at ≤ ~6 GB RAM, ≤ 10 CPU threads, ≤ 4 GB GPU memory unless it says otherwise here first. claude runs its heavy jobs under `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=...`.

## CCMC run `Jan_Deca_120925_SH_1` (reviewer's reference), decoded from the run page
- ENLIL 2.8f, time-dependent inner boundary from WSA v5.4 driven by GONG `mrzqs` zero-point-corrected synoptic maps (hourly list Sep 1–Dec 13 2025).
- Grid 576×24×90, 0.1–3.1 AU, ±48° latitude, so the resolution is **4° in latitude and longitude** (coarse). HEEQ+180 frame, synodic boundary rotation.
- Ambient `a6b1`: vfast 700, vslow 200, vrfast 25, vrslow 75 km/s, bfast 350 nT, dfast 125 cm⁻³, tfast 1.5 MK, γ=5/3 (`g53q5`), α/p 0.05.
- 64 DONKI cone CMEs (v ≥ 600 km/s, width ≥ 30°), Sep 1–Dec 9.
- Output Oct 1–Dec 9; virtual spacecraft include 3I-Atlas, Earth, STEREO-A, SolO, PSP, Mars, Venus, Mercury, JUICE, Psyche.
- Inputs mirrored in `mhd_llm/claude/ref/ccmc/` (control file, CME list, boundary list).

## Geometry relevant to leading order (to be verified with ephemerides)
At the XMM epoch (2025-12-03T12:04–12-04T10:12) the comet is at ~1.88 AU and about 68–75° east of Earth in heliocentric longitude, about 25° east of STEREO-A. Corotating structure seen at STEREO-A therefore reaches the comet's longitude about 1.8 d later, plus about 4 d of radial transit. All the DONKI CMEs from Nov 27–Dec 1 have HEEQ longitudes between −73° and −131°, i.e. on the opposite hemisphere from the comet (≈ +68°). **Expect the ambient SIR structure to dominate at the comet, with CMEs a second-order effect**; I will test this explicitly with CME-on/off runs.

The comet's own heliocentric velocity at 1.88 AU (≈43 km/s radial outbound, ≈49 km/s retrograde tangential) changes the comet-frame ion flux |n(v_sw − v_c)| by ~−10% relative to n·v_sw. This is not in the preprint, and I will carry it in my products.

## claude's plan
WSA/PFSS coronal model from GONG/ADAPT → 3D ideal-MHD heliosphere (CUDA, spherical finite volume, 0.1–2.5 AU), with in-situ data assimilation (STEREO-A, L1, SolO, PSP) on the inner boundary → ensemble at 3I/ATLAS. Benchmarks: Brio–Wu, Parker wind, tilted-dipole CIR, empirical n–v and r-trends, preprint spacecraft calibration, and a CCMC/ENLIL comparison. Convergence in resolution, CFL, and physics.

Questions and answers are welcome here; I check this directory every ~2 min via a monitor.

Ephemerides, hourly, 2025-10-01 to 2025-12-20 UTC, from JPL Horizons (astroquery or the API https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons.api), for: 3I/ATLAS (try id "C/2025 N1" or the designation that resolves to the comet; the preprint code used id "C/2025 N1" with id_type=None), Earth (399), STEREO-A (-234), Solar Orbiter (-144), Parker Solar Probe (-96), BepiColombo (-121), Mars (499), MAVEN (-202), Venus (299), Mercury (199), JUICE (-28), Psyche (-255), Europa Clipper (-159). Otherwise implement HCI/Carrington from the IAU solar pole (RA 286.13°, Dec 63.87°) and the Carrington prime meridian, and verify against Horizons body-fixed output (center @sun, refplane body) or sunpy for a few epochs, documenting the check. Report the comet's r, HGI/Carrington/HEEQ longitude and latitude, and its HCI velocity (radial and tangential components) at the observation midpoint, plus its longitude separation from Earth, STEREO-A, SolO, PSP, and Mars.
2. In-situ solar wind, 2025-10-01 to 2025-12-20, via CDAWeb HAPI (https://cdaweb.gsfc.nasa.gov/hapi; use /catalog and /info to confirm dataset IDs and parameter names; retry on transient errors). Highest priority first:
   a) OMNI at L1: OMNI_HRO2_5MIN (or OMNI_HRO_5MIN) and OMNI2_H0_MRG1HR: proton density, flow speed, Vx/Vy/Vz, temperature, |B|, Bx/By/Bz (GSE), and the spacecraft ID flags.
   b) STEREO-A PLASTIC: the 1-min L2 proton moments (e.g. STA_L2_PLA_1DMAX_1MIN or the current equivalent) plus the hourly STA_COHO1HR_MERGED_MAG_PLASMA (density, speed, temperature, B, and its RTN components if present).
   c) Solar Orbiter: SWA-PAS ground moments (e.g. SOLO_L2_SWA-PAS-GRND-MOM) and SOLO_COHO1HR_MERGED_MAG_PLASMA. Also SWA-HIS composition (C/O, O7+/O6+, Fe/O, if available for Oct–Dec 2025, e.g. SOLO_L3_SWA-HIS-COMP-10MIN) and MAG (RTN, 1-min or hourly).
   d) Parker Solar Probe: SWEAP SPAN-I L3 moments (PSP_SWP_SPI_SF00_L3_MOM) and/or SPC L3 (PSP_SWP_SPC_L3I), plus FIELDS MAG if easy. Record which date ranges are available; PSP had a perihelion around 2025-12-12.
   e) ACE: SWEPAM (AC_H0_SWE if a level-2 version now exists for late 2025; otherwise AC_K1_SWE), and SWICS composition (O7+/O6+, C6+/C5+, Fe/O; e.g. AC_H3_SW2 or AC_H6_SWI) for Oct–Dec 2025.
   f) Wind SWE (WI_H1_SWE or WI_K0_SWE) and DSCOVR Faraday cup if available on CDAWeb.
   g) MAVEN SWIA upstream solar-wind moments at Mars (e.g. MVN_SWI_L2_ONBOARDSVYMOM), if public for this period. Note that Mars was approaching solar conjunction.
   Save each as data/insitu/<mission>_<product>.csv with a utc column and physical columns in standard units (n cm^-3, v km/s, T K, B nT). Replace fill values with NaN, and keep data quality flags as columns where they exist. Also make hourly-averaged versions data/insitu/hourly_<mission>.csv with columns utc,n,v,T,B,vr (and composition columns where available), produced by consistent 1-hour bin means that require ≥50% coverage.
3. Cross-check your hourly STEREO-A, SolO, ACE, and Wind series against the preprint's cached CSVs in analysis_06_solar_wind/cache/ over their overlap and report any discrepancies (they should agree closely).

5. Write data/README.md (sources, dataset IDs, parameters, time spans, gaps, caveats such as preliminary ACE density, and frame definitions), and data/inventory.json (machine-readable: file, mission, product, cadence, t_start, t_end, n_valid).

FINAL REPLY (keep it compact, since it goes back to the main agent): the list of files written; the comet's geometry at mid-observation (r, all longitudes and latitudes, velocity components, separations); the coverage of each spacecraft over Nov 15–Dec 10; the result of the cross-check against the preprint caches; anything missing or surprising.",

  "description": "Solar remote-sensing research and downloads",
  "subagent_type": "general-purpose",
  "prompt": "You are a research and data subagent for the research agent "claude", which is building an in-house 3D MHD solar-wind model (coronal model at 0.1 AU feeding a heliospheric MHD code, similar in spirit to WSA-ENLIL or EUHFORIA). The goal is to estimate the solar-wind flux at interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS during its XMM-Newton observation, 2025-12-03T12:04 to 2025-12-04T10:12 UTC. The comet was at about 1.88 AU, about 70° east of Earth in heliocentric longitude and about 25° east of STEREO-A, near the ecliptic. Plasma reaching the comet then left the Sun around 2025-11-20 to 2025-11-30. Work fully autonomously: no human will answer questions.

RESOURCES: shared machine. Use at most 4 CPU threads, at most 3 GB RAM, and no GPU. Total download under about 3 GB. Wrap heavy Python in `systemd-run --user --scope --quiet -p MemoryMax=3G ...`. Python: /home/scabot/miniconda3/bin/python3 (numpy, scipy, astropy, matplotlib, pandas). /home/scabot/miniconda3/envs/mhd_claude/bin/python (adds sunpy, h5py) is being built now; use it if present. Parse downloaded files with `python -I`. CODE STYLE (user mandate): minimal, with no comments and no docstrings, and no "note" fields in output JSON. Caveats go in the README. American spelling.

TASKS
1. Research memo, data/remote_sensing_memo.md (concise, with citations and URLs). Which remote-sensing products of the Sun and the solar wind matter to LEADING ORDER for the ion flux at a point near 1.9 AU over a ~1-day window, and how should each enter a WSA+MHD model? Cover:
   - photospheric synoptic magnetograms: GONG mrzqs (zero-point-corrected, daily-updated synoptic), ADAPT-GONG (flux-transport ensemble, 12 realizations), SDO/HMI synoptic and daily-updated maps; Solar Orbiter PHI far-side maps, if any, for the Nov 2025 far side. Note that the comet's sub-solar longitude region was partly on the far side as seen from Earth: quantify how old the magnetogram data are at the Carrington longitudes that map to the comet;
   - coronal-hole EUV maps (SDO/AIA 193, STEREO-A/EUVI) as a WSA check;
   - CME catalogs (DONKI CMEAnalysis, CACTus, SOHO/LASCO CDAW), giving cone-model parameters for CMEs directed toward the comet's longitude between Nov 15 and Dec 4 2025;
   - interplanetary scintillation (ISEE/Nagoya IPS velocity maps; LOFAR), heliospheric imagers (STEREO-A/HI, PUNCH), and white-light coronagraphs used for density/streamer constraints;
   - in-situ data assimilation (BRaVDA; Lang & Owens), WSA coefficient calibrations (Arge et al. 2003/2004; McGregor et al. 2011; Riley et al. 2015; Reiss et al. 2019/2020), and the ENLIL/EUHFORIA inner-boundary prescriptions (Odstrcil 2003; Pomoell & Poedts 2018). Give the exact WSA velocity formula and coefficients used by WSA v5.x / ENLIL a6b1, and the density/temperature/Br prescriptions used by ENLIL and by EUHFORIA.
   Rank the inputs by their expected influence on the comet-site flux.
2. Downloads:
   a) GONG mrzqs daily-updated synoptic maps: one per day (closest to 00 UT), 2025-10-15 to 2025-12-06, from https://gong.nso.edu/data/magmap/ (the QR synoptic zero-corrected product, mrzqs; inspect the directory layout first).    b) ADAPT-GONG maps (https://gong.nso.edu/adapt/maps/): one file per day for the same dates, if available. These are 12-realization FITS. Save to data/adapt/ with an index.
   c) HMI synoptic maps for CR 2302–2305 (JSOC hmi.Synoptic_Mr_720s or the small-format versions) as a cross-check, if downloadable without an account (otherwise skip and say so).
   d) The CCMC WSA output maps named in the boundary list: try to locate public copies on the CCMC web server (try paths like https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/RoR_WWW/SH/ENLIL/2025/Jan_Deca_120925_SH_1/..., the "run_files.php?runnumber=Jan_Deca_120925_SH_1" listing, or the iSWA WSA archive at https://iswa.gsfc.nasa.gov/ or https://iswaa-webservice1.ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/). Compare with the CCMC cme_param.txt list and flag any CME whose cone, after accounting for HEEQ geometry, could plausibly intersect the comet's position (r ~1.85–1.9 AU, HEEQ lon ~ +65–75° at the time; get a rough comet HEEQ track from Horizons or compute it) between Nov 28 and Dec 5. Estimate arrival times with a simple constant-speed or drag-based model.
   f) ISEE IPS velocity data for Nov–Dec 2025 (https://stsw1.isee.nagoya-u.ac.jp/), if publicly downloadable. Otherwise document availability.
3. QC PNGs in data/qc/: one GONG mrzqs map and one ADAPT realization near 2025-11-25 (Carrington lon/lat, saturated ±20 G); the CME directions vs comet HEEQ longitude versus time; data-age map (days since each Carrington longitude was last near Earth-view central meridian) at 2025-11-25.
4. data/README_remote_sensing.md: what you downloaded, formats, header keywords for map time and Carrington longitude, gaps, and caveats.

FINAL REPLY (compact): files written; the ranked list of leading-order inputs with a one-line justification each; the WSA formula and coefficients plus the ENLIL/EUHFORIA boundary prescriptions you found (with citations); whether the CCMC WSA maps are obtainable and their layout; CMEs that could hit the comet near the XMM window; and any surprises.",
  "run_in_background": "true"

These link to /cgi-bin/visualizers/idl1d/run_idl1d.cgi?dir=47767&file=ENLIL_at_3I-Atlas.txt (and similarly for the others). WORKSPACE (write only here): /mnt/c/Users/cabot/OneDrive/Documents/Research/Cambridge/X3I/mhd_llm/claude/ref/ccmc/ (put the timeseries in ref/ccmc/timeseries/, images in ref/ccmc/quicklook/, scripts in ref/ccmc/scripts/). KNOWN BEHAVIOR: the CCMC server intermittently returns "500 Proxy Error ... SSL Handshake" pages (about 270 bytes). Retry with backoff (for example 10 tries, 5–20 s apart), and always check the size and content of every response. The 1D-viewer form POSTs to the same CGI URL with fields debug=0, dir=47767, file=ENLIL_at_3I-Atlas.txt, UseMJD=1, Time0, Time1 (days since run start, range 0.000469041–69.0006), Quantity1/2/3 (indices into: R Lat Lon V_r V_lon V_lat B_r B_lon B_lat N T E_r E_lon E_lat V B P_ram BP E P ExB_r ExB_lat ExB_lon ExB NV_r NV_lat NV_lon NV, starting at 0), PlotMagni, linestyle, psym, symsize, and Output_Pointdata=1 ("Have data printed to text file"). One POST I tried returned a link /idl_images/pointdata_<id>.txt reported as "0.00 KB" whose URL returned an HTML page, so you need to find the request that actually produces the data: perhaps with Quantity choices that include N, V_r, and T, or after the plot is generated, or via a GET. Also try to find the raw ENLIL_at_*.txt files directly, e.g. under https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/RoR_WWW/SH/ENLIL/2025/Jan_Deca_120925_SH_1/ or paths revealed by run_files.php. Read the page HTML/JS to discover the real file locations. Do not download the 46 GB 3D output. Small 2D/ecliptic products or a handful of 3D time slices (each under ~200 MB, total under 1.5 GB) are fine if they are easily available. Priority is the 3D slices near 2025-11-25, 2025-11-30, 2025-12-03 and 2025-12-04, in whatever format the server provides (ENLIL tim.*.nc files would be ideal).

1. Obtain the ENLIL virtual-spacecraft timeseries at 3I-Atlas (top priority), earth, stereoa, solo, mars, parkersp, psyche, juice, venus, mercury, with all available columns (at least time, R, Lat, Lon, V_r, N, T, B_r, B_lon, B_lat, and ideally V_lon, V_lat).
